rows: Standard reference line for global time (GMT/UTC)
Boundary determining change of calendar date
Straight line from North Pole to South Pole
Zigzagged line in the ocean to avoid splitting land territories

items: Crossing the International Date Line from West to East gains a day, while crossing from East to West loses a day.
The 82.5° E IST meridian passes through five Indian states: Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, and Andhra Pradesh.
The IDL is not a straight line; it zigzags to avoid landmasses and prevent different dates within the same island group or country.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Earth rotates 360° in 24 hours, meaning it moves 15° every hour or 1° every 4 minutes.
The International Date Line (IDL) is situated approximately along the 180° longitude in the Pacific Ocean.
Crossing the International Date Line changes the calendar date by exactly one day.
Indian Standard Time (IST) is derived from 82.5° E longitude passing near Mirzapur, maintaining UTC+05:30.
